Quick KMS note for the one‑pager: we integrate with customer KMS via CloudKMS and offer HSM-backed envelope encryption for tenant keys; control plane secrets are stored in an internal HSM cluster with audited access. We do not persist customer plaintext.

I’ll sanitize diagrams to remove internal hostnames and capacity details. ETA for sanitized package: EOD Wed (11/5).

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questionnaire: network segmentation, isolation models, and threat summary

Jack — thanks for the patience. Please find attached the requested artifacts: 1) redwood_network_isolation_v1.pdf — sanitized high‑level network isolation diagram; 2) redwood_threat_model_summary_2025.docx — one‑page threat model summary for hosted mode; 3) access-control-diagram.svg — condensed RBAC/ephemeral identity flow.

Highlights (short):
- Isolation model: control plane (managed VPC) is logically and network‑segmented from tenant compute (customer VPCs). Tenant VPCs are isolated by default; we support optional private connectivity (VPC peering/privatelink) and strict egress controls.
- Threat mitigations: mTLS for all inter‑service comms, default deny NSGs, continuous detection (IDS + anomaly scoring), and verified supply‑chain provenance for model artifacts.
- KMS: we support customer BYOK via envelope encryption (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Control plane keys are HSM backed; we provide audit logs for key usage and rotation.

Next steps: we can run a 30 minute walk‑through on Friday 11/7 or next week — booked a 30 minute slot on your calendar (link: https://cal.com/redwood/meet/sofia/30min). If you need SOC2 evidence or penetration testing reports, we’ll provide an NDA‑protected link and coordinate an evidence transfer with our compliance team.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
